Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Hey team — after we followed the migration guide and pinned to the new recommended embeddings model, our index writes started failing at ingest. Getting a dimension mismatch from our vector DB. Error: "422 EmbeddingDimensionMismatch: expected 1536, got 768". Started ~1h after the pin. Anyone seen this? :confused:

Jules M. (Support): Thanks for the report Eli — can you paste the exact request you sent (model name + small example input) and the raw error response? Also which DB are you writing to (we talk to Pinecone/Weaviate/FAISS patterns differently).

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): We call Redwood via Python SDK, short repro below. Writing into managed Pinecone. Small repro: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
res = rc.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-lite@v2", input=["hello world"])
print(res.data[0].embedding)
```
The response array length is 768 (len(...) == 768). Pinecone rejects our upsert with: "vector size mismatch: index expects 1536". We were previously on `rwd-embed-lite@v1` and had 1536 dims. We pinned to @v2 because the console suggested it.

Sam K. (Support): Hmm thanks. Two quick checks: 1) confirm the model id returned by the API exactly (sometimes alias -> different variant). 2) make sure the SDK didn't fall back to an on-device local embedder (rare but seen in customer envs). Can you run the curl for definiteness and paste the headers/response (no API key)?

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Pasted curl output (sanitized): 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{"model":"rwd-embed-lite@v2","input":"hello"}
200 OK
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...] , "object":"embedding"}], "model":"rwd-embed-lite@v2", "usage":{...}}
```
Length of the array is 768.

Jules M. (Support): Ok that's clear. Two likely root causes: either the model variant `rwd-embed-lite@v2` intentionally changed architecture/dim or there's a bug in the alias that pointed customers to a smaller test variant. I'm escalating to Eng-ML for confirmation. Priya, can you check model catalog entry for rwd-embed-lite@v2 and recent rollout notes?

Priya Nair (Eng-ML): Looking now. Confirmed: upstream training pushed a new quantized variant `rwd-embed-lite@v2-q8` for lower-cost usage which outputs 768-d embeddings. The alias `rwd-embed-lite@v2` should have pointed to the 1536-d float variant but an infra routing mislabel caused late traffic to the q8 variant. We're seeing a small fraction of customers routed to q8 if they hit certain capacity pools.

Priya Nair (Eng-ML): Root cause: model alias assignment + capacity routing. We introduced the q8 variant yesterday and a config diff caused the alias metadata to reference the wrong variant in some regions.

Sam K. (Support): OK — that's consistent with Eli's symptoms. Immediate mitigation options for the customer: 
- Re-pin to the explicit full-dimension model version: `rwd-embed-lite@v2-float` (this avoids alias resolution).
- Or roll back to `rwd-embed-lite@v1` if you need immediate stability and then reindex later.
- Short-term workaround: if you must keep current vectors and are blocked, you can re-create vectors by requesting embedding with the explicit float model and re-upserting. Padding/truncating vectors to match dims is unsafe and not recommended.

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Thanks. If we reindex to the 1536-d vectors, Pinecone will accept. Problem is we have ~850k vectors — reindexing time/cost is nontrivial. Is there any plan to map/expand 768->1536 deterministically?

Priya Nair (Eng-ML): Not reliably; you can't expand 768->1536 meaningfully. We can offer to temporarily pin routing on our side for your org so that your requests go to the float variant (no reindex) while we fix the alias globally. That would preserve existing vectors and restore expected dims. If you prefer that, tell us the org ID and we'll apply a routing override.

Jules M. (Support): Eli — want us to do the routing override? If yes, confirm org ID + region and we'll make the change and verify via a quick smoke test (return embedding length).

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Yes please — org ID: acme-9876, region: us-east-1. Would appreciate the override while we plan reindexing. Also curious: any automation we should add to catch this earlier?

Sam K. (Support): We'll apply the override and post back when done. For automation: we recommend adding a lightweight check in your ingestion pipeline that asserts embedding length == expected_dim before upsert and fails fast with a clear alert to SRE. That way you block-fail before paying for large failed upsert attempts. Also subscribe to model catalog change-notifications (Console -> Settings -> Model Alerts).

deploy-bot: scheduled change: apply-routing-override org=acme-9876 region=us-east-1 target_model=rwd-embed-lite@v2-float ETA=now

Priya Nair (Eng-ML): override applied, confirmed routing for acme-9876 -> rwd-embed-lite@v2-float in us-east-1. Can you re-run your small curl test?

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Re-ran curl — embedding length is 1536 now. Pinecone upsert accepted. 🙏 :tada:

Jules M. (Support): Great — leaving notes: - Root cause: alias->variant misassignment caused some traffic to q8 768-d variant - Short-term: routing override applied for acme-9876 - Medium-term: Eng-ML to fix alias metadata and add a unit test to prevent variant aliasing per-region - Action item for customer: schedule reindex if you want all vectors produced by the same model (optional)

Priya Nair (Eng-ML): Action items (internal): 1) Roll out alias fix and validate across regions; 2) Add automated alert when model alias points to a variant with different vector_size metadata; 3) Add console warning when users attempt to pin to an alias that has mixed variants. I'll follow up in eng-ml channel and link to this thread.

Eli Chen (Acme Integrations): Appreciate the fast response. Leaving this thread open until alias fix is global, but override works for now.

Jules M. (Support): Thanks Eli — we'll keep it open and update when the global fix is deployed. :thumbsup:
